comment: The same pattern in financing. The draft says "only one genuinely new DPI-H component emerges from the financing analysis: the Benefits Package Registry," and its appendix places the Contract & Benefits Management System — which "processes claims and contributions" — explicitly outside DPI-H, as a "functional application." We agree the processing belongs there. But a claim also runs a lifecycle across autonomous payers and providers — coverage/eligibility, pre-authorisation, submission, adjudication, settlement — and nothing owns the shared exchange that carries it between them and flags a stall. That exchange — protocol, directory, trust, governance — is the fabric we mean; adjudication and payment stay with the parties (a DPI-H construct on the refined criterion in C2). We are not asking for the claims-processing system to be DPI-H, and this is not a central claims switch. We recommend recognising the shared claims-exchange fabric as a DPI-H construct. One fabric idea covers coordination and claims.
